title: Physics Tutorial - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Physics is the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, force, and the laws governing the universe. It explains natural phenomena ranging from the motion of planets and flow of electricity to the behavior of light, heat, sound, atoms, and subatomic particles.

Physics forms the foundation of modern science and technology and plays an important role in engineering, medicine, electronics, communication, transportation, and space exploration.

Why Should We Learn Physics?

Physics reveals how everything works, from tiny atoms to the vast universe. It explains fundamental principles and solves real-world problems.

  • Blue Sky & Day/Night: Physics explains why the sky is blue and why we have day and night.
  • GPS: The phone in your hand uses orbiting satellites and physics principles to track your location.
  • Ball in a Moving Bus: Drop a ball on a bus? It falls straight down to you because you, the ball, and the bus all move together.
  • Electric Shock: Ohm's Law explains how current passing through the body causes shocks, with circuit breakers controlling resistance to prevent accidents.
  • Microwave Oven: Physics principles of electromagnetic waves are used in microwave ovens to heat food quickly and efficiently.
  • Smartphone Touchscreen: Capacitive touchscreens in smartphones work based on the principles of electrical conductivity and charge transfer.
  • Solar Panels: Physics explains how solar cells convert sunlight into electricity, providing clean energy.
  • Airplane Flight: Physics explains how the lift generated by the wings of an airplane allows it to stay airborne and navigate through the sky.

Mechanics

Mechanics deals with the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.

  • Motion
  • Distance and Displacement
  • Speed and Velocity
  • Acceleration
  • Newton’s Laws of Motion
  • Friction
  • Gravitation
  • Rotational Motion

Properties of Matter

This branch studies the physical properties and behavior of solids and fluids.

  • Elasticity
  • Fluids Pressure
  • Viscosity
  • Surface Tension
  • Capillary Action
  • Hooke's Law
  • Young's Modulus
  • Bulk Modulus
  • Bernoulli's Principle

Heat and Thermodynamics

Thermodynamics studies heat, temperature, work, and energy transformations.

  • Heat Transfer (Conduction, Convection & Radiation)
  • Thermal Expansion
  • Laws of Thermodynamics (Zeroth, First, Second & Third Law)
  • Heat Engine
  • Entropy
  • Refrigeration

Oscillations and Waves

Oscillations involve repetitive motion around an equilibrium position, while waves transfer energy through a medium or space.

  • Simple Harmonic Motion
  • Amplitude, Frequency and Time Period
  • Wave Motion
  • Doppler Effect
  • Resonance

Electrostatics and Current Electricity

This branch studies electric charges, electric fields, and electric current.

  • Electric Charge
  • Coulomb’s Law
  • Electric Field
  • Electric Potential
  • Ohm’s Law
  • Kirchhoff’s Laws
  • Resistivity
  • Wheatstone Bridge

Magnetism and Electromagnetic Induction

Magnetism studies magnetic fields produced by moving charges, while electromagnetic induction explains how changing magnetic fields produce electric current.

  • Magnetic Field
  • Electromagnets
  • Lorentz Force
  • Faraday’s Law
  • Lenz’s Law
  • Magnetic Flux
  • Transformers and Generators

Ray Optics and Wave Optics

Optics studies the behavior and properties of light.

  • Reflection of Light
  • Laws of Reflection
  • Refraction
  • Mirrors
  • Lenses
  • Total Internal Reflection
  • Dispersion
  • Interference
  • Diffraction
  • Polarization
  • Young’s Double Slit Experiment
  • Scattering of Light and Tyndall Effect

Modern Physics

Modern Physics explains the behavior of matter and energy at atomic and subatomic levels.

Atoms and Nuclei

  • Atomic Models
  • Atomic Spectra
  • Radioactivity
  • Types of Radioactivity: Alpha, Beta, Gamma Decay
  • Nuclear Reactions
  • Nuclear Energy

Quantum Mechanics

  • Photoelectric Effect
  • Dual Nature of Matter
  • de Broglie Hypothesis
  • Einstein’s Photoelectric Equation

Semiconductor Electronics

Semiconductor Physics forms the basis of modern electronic devices.

  • Semiconductors
  • Conductors and Insulators
  • Diodes
  • Transistors
  • Logic Gates
  • Boolean Algebra
  • Classification of Energy Bands
  • Intrinsic Semiconductors and Extrinsic Semiconductors
  • Forward Bias
  • Reverse Bias

Communication Systems

Communication systems enable the transmission of information over long distances.

  • Communication System
  • Elements of the Communication Process
  • What is Noise Factor?
  • Attenuation
  • What is Modulation?
  • Difference between Modulation and Demodulation
